artist_reel_line: Lotus Glow was Bandcamp's Album of the Day; in 2026, The Nightlife.
Living Thing in 2024, Animal Poem in 2025; this fall, West Coast dates with Margaret Glaspy.

Dog Eared went to No. 1 on the UK folk chart; then her own North America and UK tour.
Johnny Cash covered his title song; in 2026, We Are Together Again.
Fools Parade on New West in 2024; by fall 2026, still on the circuit at OffBeat in Reno.
Four ARIAs and a Grammy nod in 2015; in 2026, Newport Folk and the Sydney Opera House.

A decade as Seattle's best-kept secret; then Saddle Creek and a tour with Rilo Kiley.

An Americana Emerging Act nominee in 2019; in fall 2026, Europe and the record Banquet Rock.

Willamette Week's best new bands in March 2024; in spring 2026, the Portland Jazz Festival.

A record with Katie Crutchfield as Plains; in October 2026, A Mile South of Heaven.

Apprenticed with George Gibson; his banjo is on Tyler Childers' Grammy-nominated album.

A Youth Poet Laureate whose debut was The Line of Best Fit's No. 1; in 2026, The Mountain.

Born in a hotel lobby band; days after Pickathon, a debut on Verve.
Daughter of Portland's First Lady of the Blues; in June 2026, Only a Drop.

Called HillBillie Holiday; Borned in Ya, then an album with Theo Lawrence in 2026.

On the farm in 2024; then Cerca del Lugar in 2025.

Curyman, with Arthur Verocai's strings; Curyman II took him to the Holland Festival.

Guard Dog found its listeners online; in January 2026, Death in the Business of Whaling.

Sisters singing mid-century country and doo-wop; then Rollercoasters in 2025.

Seattle funk and soul; since then, halls in the Netherlands.
Two voices and a fiddle since 2020; Modern Cowboy in 2023, and in 2026, Porchlight.
